newsitem.title: UK: SW Trains confident of meeting OPRAF targets.
newsitem.headline: SW Trains confident of meeting OPRAF targets.

text.p: British railway franchise South West Trains, a unit of Stagecoach Holdings Plc, said on Tuesday it was gradually leaving its days of poor performance behind and was confident of meeting future targets of rail regulators.
SW Trains got a reprieve from paying a fine of one million stg earlier this month by meeting its performance target for April set by the Office of Passenger Rail (OPRAF).
SW Trains' chairman and managing director Brian Cox told Reuters that the company was happy with its progress so far in May. "We expect to maintain the target," he said.

SW Trains maintained a 99.6 percent running level in April after it faced criticism for cancelling a number of services in February and March after job reductions left it with too few drivers to operate new shift schedules.
Cox said 15 drivers have been retained long-term who, according to earlier plans, were facing redundancy.
"There will be 100 new journeys this summer," said Cox, reiterating that the operator was confident of regaining passenger confidence.
The train operator announced earlier on Tuesday that it would be ordering 30 new trains to rejuvenate its fleet of 120 "slam door" trains.

The electric four-car trains will be built in Britain by GEC-Alsthom -- a joint venture of Britain's General Electric Co Plc and France's Alcatel Alsthom -- for Porterbrook Leasing Co Ltd and will be leased to SW Trains.
The first of the new trains will go on rails in late 1998, with all of them expected to come on track in regular phases by 2000.
SW Trains' move to replace just 30 trains faced flak from pressure group Save our Railways which criticised it for not replacing other "slam door" trains.
Cox said it was difficult to replace more than 30 trains during the current seven-year franchise term but would like to see them replaced faster than expected if the term was renewed.
The current franchise to operate trains in the south west of UK, owned by Stagecoach, is about 15 months old.
"We have also committed about a million pounds towards station improvement," Cox said. He said SW Trains will shortly announce a package of passenger benefits.
